22|Other Safety Endpoints
23|Other safety endpoints include selected adverse events (AEs), serious adverse events (SAEs),
24|and certain laboratory parameters (serum creatinine and calcitonin; see Section 4.6.3) and vital
25|signs (see Section 4.6.4). Adverse events will be monitored over the course of the trial,
26|starting from the time of randomization and through the duration of the patient's participation,
27|including the 70 day post treatment follow-up period. Adverse events reported by the patient
28|will be evaluated by the investigator to determine if a given event meets the criteria for a
29|serious event. An adverse event that does not meet the definition of a serious event will be
30|considered non-serious and will not be collected, with the exception of potential clinical
31|events (non-serious AEs) and expected events of diabetic complication (for details see
32|protocol Section 10.3).
33|4.
34|ANALYSIS METHODS
35|4.1
36|General Principles
37|In addition to specific analyses and presentations that are detailed in the following sections,
38|results will be summarized for continuous measures using descriptive statistics, including the
39|number of patients, mean, standard deviation, median and range as appropriate. For natural
40|logarithm transformed data, geometric mean, standard error of the geometric mean will also
41|be provided. For categorical variables counts and percentage per treatment group will be
42|presented.
43|For all time-to event analyses, the treatment groups will be analyzed using a Cox proportional
44|hazards model that includes treatment as an explanatory factor unless specified otherwise.
45|Prior CV event group at randomization from the IVRS randomization strata (prior CV event
46|or no prior CV event, refer to "Prior CV event at randomization based on IVRS" in short) will
47|be included as a stratification factor. The Efron method1 will be used for handling ties. P-value

22|For all time to event analysis of composite endpoints including mortality, if the death occurred
23|after 6 months from the last visit where all components of the endpoint could be assessed, the
24|death will not be counted towards any composite endpoint where death is a component.
25|Instead, such patients will be censored in accordance with the relevant censoring scheme. For
26|analysis of mortality as an endpoint, such deaths will be counted as events. Unless otherwise
27|specified all hypothesis testing will be performed using two-sided tests at the 0.05 level of
28|significance. Statistical analyses will be performed using Version 9.2 (or newer) of SASon
29|Unix operating system.
30|Selected analyses described here will be summarized separately for the US and the China
31|population respectively.
32|4.1.1
33|Control of Type I Error
34|Type I error will be controlled at a one-sided 0.025 level for multiplicity across primary and
35|secondary objectives and in consideration of planned interim analyses. The alpha of 0.02495
36|represents the final one-sided significance level to be used when the study has been completed
37|in entirety. At an interim analysis, testing for superiority of primary efficacy endpoint will
38|occur, and the significance level for superiority will be replaced by one-sided 0.00005 at the
39|first and one-sided 0.0005 at the second interim (see Section 4.7). Statistical testing will
40|proceed sequentially and statistical significance will be assessed in the following hierarchical
41|order. When a test is found to be statistically significant, testing will proceed to the next test.
42|If a test is not statistically significant, the subsequent one will not be assessed for statistical
43|significance although nominal p-values will be provided.
44|Hierarchical Testing Order:

27|Non-inferiority will be tested only at the completion of the study. Secondary endpoints will

34|Censoring
35|4.1.2.1
36|Censoring Scheme
37|Primary Censoring Scheme: in time-to-event analyses in the ITT population, patients will be
38|censored at the earliest of: 1) date of last contact where all elements of the endpoint could be
39|assessed, and 2) the right censoring date. The conclusions regarding non-inferiority or
40|superiority will be based on the analyses using this censoring scheme. Patients without any
41|assessment of the endpoint will be censored at randomization.
42|On-treatment Censoring Scheme: in the on-treatment time-to-event analyses, patients will be
43|censored at the earliest of: 1) date of last contact where all elements of the endpoint could be

6|assessed, and 2) the date of last dose of study medication, and 3) the right censoring date.
7|Patients who never start the study drug will be censored at randomization.
8|On-treatment + n days Censoring Scheme (where n=7, 30, and 70): patients will be censored
9|at the earliest of: 1) date of last contact where all elements of the endpoint could be assessed,
10|2) the date of last dose of study medication + n days, and 3) the right censoring date. Patients
11|who never start the study drug will be censored at randomization.
12|Cut-off Date Censoring Scheme: patients will be censored at the earliest of: 1) date of last
13|contact where all elements of the endpoint could be assessed, and 2) the primary endpoint cut
14|off date. The primary endpoint cut off date will be determined by the Executive Committee as
15|the date when the sites will start bringing patients back for the Trial Termination visit. Patients
16|without any assessment of the endpoint will be censored at randomization.
17|Right censoring date is defined as the last known alive date as collected at the trial termination
18|visit (TTV form) except for deceased patients where it is the adjudicated date of the death.
19|4.1.2.2
20|Assumption on Non-informative Censoring
21|The time to event analysis (Cox regression) relies on the assumption of non-informative
22|censoring. To examine this assumption, variables that may be related to censoring, for
23|example, the most frequent major protocol deviation, certain SAEs, will be explored. Rates
24|per 100 patient-years will be calculated per treatment group and compared between patients
25|censored early without complete follow-up, and those with complete follow-up.
26|To assess possible effects of informative censoring on the primary efficacy endpoint,
27|sensitivity analyses will be done as follows. First, the tipping point analysis will be performed
28|where in patients who prematurely discontinued the study without having a primary endpoint
29|event prior to discontinuation, events will be imputed during their missing follow up time (i.e.
30|time from censoring to trial termination visit) under various scenarios for the hazard rates for
31|non-completers in each arm. For each scenario, 2000 imputations will be performed and the
32|results will be combined across 2000 combined datasets (actual events in completers +
33|imputed events in non-completers) using SAS PROC MIANALYZE. Specifically, log-hazard
34|ratio estimate of treatment effect will be calculated as an average and its associated variance
35|will be obtained using Rubin's8 (1987) formula, which combines within-imputation and
36|between-imputation variances. Hazard ratios, Wald's 95% CIs and Wald's test p-values will
37|also be calculated. The goal of this analysis is to find scenarios where the primary analysis
38|results will be "tipped", i.e. the conclusion will change.
39|4.2
40|Study Conduct
41|Major protocol deviations will be identified for all patients who are randomized (see Section
42|2.2).
